MODEL REVIEW (claude-opus-5-5, a model and not a human, 2026-11-05; reviewed_by stays null): Checked the 10 Facts, the stop path, native.py, the fake, scope, licence and risk against the clone at the pin and the UR dashboard manual it ships (resources/DashboardServer_e-Series.pdf); the author's pass rested on defects: UR_DASHBOARD.send_command catches every exception and returns None (ur_dashboard.py:58-87), so the power_off e-stop, the stop_program safe-state action and pause completed with a dead socket and reads silently dropped a field; the safe state claimed 'arm powered off' while its only action stopped a URP program and no stop was confirmed by state; the re-enable ran the whole initialize(), which unlocks protective stops, restarts safety (emergency-stop states included), switches MANUAL to automatic and releases the brakes (ur_dashboard.py:96-134), against the manual's inspect-first warnings and the card's note that brake release is never a model command without an operator; and the run_urp_program and UR-constructor Facts said more than their lines. In driver.py the reviewer made the e-stop fail on an unanswered power off, added the safe-state action x-cap.ad-sdl.power_off.v1 (power off, then fresh robotmode reads until POWER_OFF within 5 s, else SAFE_STATE_UNREACHED), made stop_program an ordinary latched command, made pause and stop complete only on the manual's 'Pausing program' and 'Stopped' and every read fail on a None answer, rewrote the re-enable x-cap.ad-sdl.power_on.v1 as permit-gated (only with safety status NORMAL: the upstream brake_release from POWER_OFF, BOOTING, POWER_ON or IDLE, confirmed RUNNING by a fresh read; never an unlock, safety restart or mode switch), rewrote safe_state, descriptions and the docstring, corrected six Facts and added eleven (send_command, the getters, radians from README.md:65-69 and keyboard_control.py, its stopl stop, restart_safety, the licence). The fake now answers the manual's texts, None as a swallowed socket error and refuses a move unless RUNNING (fake.py); twelve package cases replace four (test_driver.py); native.py's docstring states the hazards of the constructor's initialize(); facts.md was rewritten and reference.json, REFERENCE.md and check-report.json regenerated. Blocked SDK_BUG: the permit-gated re-enable fails only G8 SAFE-031, which needs a second distinct valid input for the only gated capability while CORE-086 makes a re-enable input-free (TSAFE-001 itself handles permit-gated re-enables); without requires_permit the package passed G8 and all twelve cases on a scratch copy, so the orchestrator chooses between fixing SAFE-031 and an unpermitted re-enable (the xArm precedent, which the card's brake-release note argues against). The author's notes on a pass, the initialize() re-enable and stop_program as the safe state are superseded; RESULT.json catalogue_requests still lack x-cap.ad-sdl.power_off.v1 and describe power_on and stop_program as before; gate digest sha256:657ce2bce321e6694e3c4ebb6bf8fb5969c1649f8fb6250c028a10b28041c841 (failed G8). The card needs the owner's publication decision (publish_review required; licence MIT); the package may not be published or merged into a published tree before it. For the human reviewer: Hardware, never run: (1) The loader opens the backend at every endpoint start (a restart with a restored latch included), and UR() runs UR_DASHBOARD.initialize(): it unlocks a protective stop, restarts safety whenever the status lacks NORMAL (emergency-stop states included), switches MANUAL to automatic (per the manual this takes mode switching from PolyScope and disables its password) and brake-releases the arm, against the manual's warnings; decide whether this backend may be opened at all. (2) The stop is a dashboard power off, the upstream's own e_stop, confirmed by a POWER_OFF robotmode read: a power cut, not a controlled deceleration; the clone implies but never states that the joint brakes hold, and says nothing of a gripper, pipette or screwdriver on the flange losing power; confirm both. (3) The manual lists power off, brake release, stop and pause as remote-control commands: in local control the MHS e-stop reports SAFE_STATE_UNREACHED and only the physical stop works; no physical stop is cited (estop_physical_ref unset). (4) The dashboard socket has no lock and no request ids; a late or crossed answer makes a stop report failure, never success. (5) home blocks in URX movej (outside the clone), so an e-stop during it stays command_in_flight until UR.home returns; the re-enable blocks 20 s in brake_release. (6) Every dashboard command prints to stdout, which corrupts an MHS stdio server. (7) run_urp_program (not bound) uploads and plays any program and its loop never ends. (8) Licence: UR's manual (reproduction needs UR's approval), Robotiq's PoC PDF and five URCaps are third-party files in an MIT clone; the override proposes publish_review required.
